newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest aluminum premium spread widens.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest aluminum premium spread widens.

text.p: The U.S. aluminum premium range widened this week amid tightness of material available for guaranteed delivery, dealers said.
The Midwest premium for guaranteed delivery was reported as high as 5.00 cents over LME cash, while chain metal premiums are believed to be 4.00 to 4.75 cents.
The LME three-month price fell $3 in the afternoon kerb to $1,697 a tonne.

"There some tightness in the Midwest," said one dealer. "Some of the producers are focusing on their downstream businesses and not as much on their primary business. So there seems to be less material available in the Midwest."
Dealers reported some flexibility in premiums because of the evaporation of the cash-to-three-month contango on the LME, which went from $28 in early July to $1 Wednesday.
"When you can't carry your position, you try to liquidate it as quickly as you can," another trader said. "So there's been a lot of people offering lower premiums."
He added that the narrowing of the spreads was "a temporary situation," and would probably widen next month.
The narrowing has been attributed to a squeeze of the August LME prompt date.

Other dealers attrbited the wide range to the LME rally. "Some traders look at the market at a fixed price basis," one merchant said. "They see LME prices at $1,700 and they figure they can give a little up on the premium."

Fundamentally, the market remains buoyant, dealers said. "I can't remember a summer that was this strong," one dealer said. "The consumers we deal with are very happy. The producers' downstream operations seem well ahead of last year."
((Derek J. Caney, New York Commodity Desk, 212-859-1646))
